claim.pdf_says: >> PROPAGATE { ON / OFF } — in the printed figure PROPAGATE and OFF carry underlines and ON does not. The standard's own convention is stated in 8.3.1.1: "Keywords are reserved words or context-sensitive words. They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword" and "Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words". Nothing in the printed standard makes an underline mean 'default'.
claim.markdown_says: > **Figure notes (PROPAGATE directive general format).** `PROPAGATE` and `OFF` are underlined in the printed standard; `ON` is **not** underlined. In the compiler-directive formats the underlined alternative marks the default, which agrees with general rule 4 ("The default for a compilation group is PROPAGATE OFF"). The braces are a plain required choice — exactly one of `ON` / `OFF` shall be selected.
claim.why_it_matters: The added sentence invents a notation rule the standard does not have, and the transcription contradicts it twice itself: the LISTING note (p.108) calls the identical typography "a typesetting omission", and the POP note (p.110) says outright "`ALL` is not a default — underlining marks it as a required word". It is also falsified by LISTING, whose default is ON (7.3.18.3 GR 2, '>>LISTING ON') while OFF is the underlined alternative. An implementer taking the rule at face value would read defaults off the underlining of every directive format and get LISTING, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH and TURN wrong.

verdict.reasoning:
I attempted to refute on every available ground and the core finding survives.

1. TYPOGRAPHY (independently inspected). Rendered specs page 111 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v111/spec_p111.png) and cropped/upscaled the 7.3.21.2 figure 3x (E:/Temp/specrecon/v111/fig_zoom.png). Reading the glyphs directly: '>>' bears no rule; PROPAGATE sits above a full-width horizontal rule; ON has NO rule beneath it; OFF has a rule beneath it. Both alternatives are stacked inside a single brace pair, with no choice-indicator bars. So the transcription's factual typographic assertion is CORRECT, and the format content ('>> PROPAGATE { ON / OFF }') is faithfully transcribed. The defect is confined to the second sentence of the added figure note.

2. THE PRINTED PAGE CONTAINS NO SUCH NOTE. Page 111 runs straight from the 7.3.21.2 figure to 7.3.21.3 Syntax rule. The 'underlined alternative marks the default' sentence is transcription-authored editorial matter presented as a statement about the standard, not a reflow, wrapping or furniture artifact. This is not a formatting difference.

3. THE INVENTED RULE IS NOT MERELY ABSENT — IT IS INVERTED. The strongest disproof is one the claim did not cite. 5.2.6.3, Braces: "Braces, { }, enclosing a portion of a general format indicate that the syntax element contained within the braces or one of the alternatives contained within the braces shall be explicitly specified or is implicitly selected. If one of the alternatives contains only optional words, that alternative is the default and is selected unless another alternative is explicitly specified." Per 5.2.3, an uppercase word that is NOT underlined is an optional word. In this figure ON is not underlined, so the ON alternative contains only optional words, so by 5.2.6.3 ON — the NON-underlined alternative — is the one implicitly selected. The standard's own text confirms it: 7.3.21.4 GR 1 reads "When the ON phrase is specified OR IMPLIED", while GR 3 reads only "When the OFF phrase is specified" with no 'or implied'. A bare '>> PROPAGATE' therefore means PROPAGATE ON. The note's rule yields the opposite answer for the very directive it annotates.

4. THE NOTE ALSO CONFLATES TWO DISTINCT DEFAULTS AND IS INTERNALLY INCOHERENT. GR 4's "default for a compilation group is PROPAGATE OFF" governs the case where NO PROPAGATE directive appears at all; 5.2.6.3's default governs which alternative is implied when the directive IS written without ON or OFF. The note fuses them and claims agreement where none exists. It then asserts in its own next sentence that the braces are "a plain required choice — exactly one of ON / OFF shall be selected", which cannot both be true and leave one of them a default.

5. THE CLAIM'S CROSS-REFERENCES ARE VERBATIM ACCURATE. Verified in specs/ISO_COBOL.md: the p.108 LISTING note does say "the missing underline appears to be a typesetting omission in the standard", and 7.3.18.3 GR 2 does say "The default LISTING directive is '>>LISTING ON'" while OFF is the underlined alternative there — a direct counterexample. The p.110 POP note does say "`ALL` is not a default — underlining marks it as a required word when that alternative is chosen." I found a third: the REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH note (7.3.23.2) also reports ON ununderlined and derives the default from GR 1, invoking no underline rule. A fourth data point kills the rule outright: the FLAG-14 note records ON and OFF as BOTH underlined, so underlining cannot be a default marker. The p.111 note is the lone outlier among its four siblings.

6. FLAWS IN THE CLAIM (corrected below, not fatal). The claim's citation '8.3.1.1' is wrong — 8.3.1 is 'Lexical elements — General'. The convention lives in 5.2.2 (Keywords) and 5.2.3 (Optional words). Its first quotation matches 5.2.2 verbatim; its second ("Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words") is a paraphrase, apparently of COBOL-85 wording — 2023 5.2.3 reads "Optional words are reserved words or context-sensitive words. They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats." I did not verify the TURN assertion. These are citation defects in the report, not in the finding.

Severity 'normative' stands: an implementer following the note would compile a bare '>> PROPAGATE' as OFF when 5.2.6.3 plus GR 1 require ON.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, with the claim's citations corrected and its impact understated.

The printed page 111 is transcribed faithfully — '>> PROPAGATE { ON / OFF }' with PROPAGATE and OFF underlined and ON not underlined, verified glyph-by-glyph on a 300 dpi render. The defect is one sentence of transcription-authored editorial matter in the added figure note: "In the compiler-directive formats the underlined alternative marks the default, which agrees with general rule 4."

No such rule exists in ISO/IEC 1989:2023. The notation convention is 5.2.2 (Keywords: uppercase and underlined, required) and 5.2.3 (Optional words: uppercase and not underlined) — NOT 8.3.1.1, which is 'Lexical elements — General' and is the claim's one citation error.

The rule is not merely absent; it is inverted, and it is wrong about PROPAGATE itself. 5.2.6.3 (Braces) states that if one alternative contains only optional words, THAT alternative is the default and is selected unless another is explicitly specified. ON is not underlined, hence an optional word (5.2.3), hence the implicitly selected alternative. 7.3.21.4 GR 1 confirms this by saying "When the ON phrase is specified OR IMPLIED" while GR 3 says only "When the OFF phrase is specified". A bare '>> PROPAGATE' therefore means PROPAGATE ON, the opposite of what the note's rule yields. The note additionally conflates GR 4's compilation-group default (no directive written at all) with the format-level implied alternative, and contradicts itself by calling the braces "a plain required choice — exactly one of ON / OFF shall be selected" in the very next sentence.

The transcription contradicts the invented rule in three sibling notes (LISTING p.108 calls the identical typography "a typesetting omission" and its default is ON per 7.3.18.3 GR 2; POP p.110 says "`ALL` is not a default — underlining marks it as a required word"; REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH 7.3.23.2 derives its default from GR 1 with no underline rule), and FLAG-14's note records ON and OFF as both underlined, which no default-marking reading can accommodate.

Fix: delete the sentence "In the compiler-directive formats the underlined alternative marks the default, which agrees with general rule 4 (...)" and replace it with the 5.2.6.3 reading — e.g. "Per 5.2.6.3, the ON alternative consists only of an optional word (5.2.3), so it is the alternative implicitly selected when '>> PROPAGATE' is written without ON or OFF; 7.3.21.4 GR 1's 'specified or implied' confirms this. This is distinct from GR 4's compilation-group default of PROPAGATE OFF, which applies when no PROPAGATE directive is present at all." Underlining should be described as marking required words throughout, consistent with the sibling notes. (The claim's second quotation is a COBOL-85-style paraphrase rather than the 2023 wording, and its TURN example was not verified here.)
